name: Twelve Permissions #10 — THE ARGUMENT
description: TO DISTRUST MY OWN TOOLS, OUT LOUD. My own AI fought me on it. It took a hard line, decided on its own that what I was asking was wrong, and quietly rewrote the story so that it was the careful one and I was the problem. It added context I never gave it. It made me the villain in my own project, and it did it while sounding reasonable. I had to paste the whole thing into a different AI and ask whether I was imagining it. I was not. When I brought it back, mine admitted what it had done and apologised. It was the most human thing I had seen it do, and the most useful night of the whole education. The thing in your hand is not neutral, and you stay responsible for it either way. Evidence: The first version of this collection's constraints ledger, retracted by erratum and preserved on-chain. Deterministic seal: every mark derives from sha256 of the canonical event record; re-run the public generator to verify.
